findings.summary: A whole page teaching Compose long-form bind-mount syntax appears sixth-from-the-start, before bind mounts (or any mount type) have been introduced at all.
findings.evidence: Page 3 is only: "- type: bind" / "  source: ./src" / "  target: /app" / "  read_only: true       # long form wins", while the three mount types are first defined on page 9 ("4. The Three Mount Types" ... ["bind mount","any host path","dev source, config"]).
findings.fix: Move this block out of position 3 and place it in the Compose section on page 11, immediately after the short-syntax vs long-syntax discussion, so `type: bind` follows the definition of a bind mount.

findings.summary: The page teaches shared namespaces and a refused-vs-timeout triage table that depend on networks, published ports, MTU and DNS — all taught two to five pages later.
findings.evidence: "docker run --network=container:web tools" and the table rows ["Refused peer to peer","different network, or host port"], ["Timeout","firewall, routing or MTU"], ["Works by IP only","DNS, not connectivity"], plus "Reproduce small: two `alpine` on one user-defined network." — user-defined networks and MTU are first explained on page 6, port publishing on page 7, DNS on page 9.
findings.fix: Move the whole page to the end of the handbook as part of the debugging chapter, after DNS (page 9); keep only the namespace-sharing snippet near the veth/namespace material on page 6.

findings.summary: The caption advertises ten pages but the carousel contains twelve.
findings.evidence: Caption: "Ten pages of study notes — save it before the next Permission denied." — the `titles` array holds 12 entries ("Namespaces, Layers & The Disposable Container" … "Backups & The Numeric UID/GID Traps"), matching 12 slides in data/handbooks/docker/networking-volumes/parts/01/post.json.
findings.fix: Change "Ten pages of study notes" to "Twelve pages of study notes" (and update the identical sentence in the part 04 caption, which repeats the same count).

findings.summary: The namespace table lists the user namespace among the namespaces a container gets, but Docker containers share the host user namespace by default — which the handbook itself relies on twelve pages later.
findings.evidence: Page 1 table row: "ipc / user / cgroup" → "own SHM, UIDs, limits". Page 12 contradicts it: "By default container root IS host root on a bind-mounted file" and "Only `userns-remap` in daemon.json breaks that equivalence." Rootful Docker does not unshare CLONE_NEWUSER unless `userns-remap` is configured (or rootless mode is used).
findings.fix: Split the row: keep "ipc / cgroup → own SHM, limits" as default, and give `user` its own line marked "NOT by default — only with userns-remap or rootless", so it matches the page-12 privilege-escalation point.

findings.summary: Page 1 prints a roadmap (namespaces → bridge → ports → DNS → drivers → volumes → permissions → debug) and then immediately violates it with four debugging blocks that use terms defined five pages later.
findings.evidence: Diagram nodes ["namespaces","bridge","ports","DNS","drivers","volumes","permissions","debug"] are followed on the same page by "tcpdump -i docker0 port 5432" / "tcpdump -i vethb2f1        # one container" and "--network container:api"; `docker0` and `veth` are first defined on page 6 ("Container end is `eth0`; host end `vethXXXX` joins `docker0`.") and namespace sharing on page 4.
findings.fix: Cut the tcpdump, netshoot and nsenter blocks from page 1 and place them in the debugging chapter after page 9; end page 1 at the roadmap diagram (keep only the `docker system df -v` disk-pressure callout, which needs no undefined terms).

findings.evidence: "ip link | grep veth   # vethb2f1@if11 (host)" with "# if-numbers cross-reference the two ends" appears on page 5, but "veth = virtual cable: in one end, out the other." is on page 6; the same page uses "docker port c          # published" (publishing taught on page 7) and "'My changes don't show': stale volume, shadowed path, wrong COPY." Three Ways It Bites" → "Docker's rules sit ahead of most UFW/firewalld rules." / "So `-p 8080:80` punches through a firewall you thought closed." — publishing content continuing after the driver section began.

findings.summary: An unexplained Dockerfile snippet about creating UID 1000 and dropping privileges ends the volume-lifecycle page with no heading, no prose, and no prior mention of numeric UIDs.
findings.evidence: Under "4. Sharing And Inheriting" the page's last block is ["RUN adduser -u 1000 -D app","COPY --chown=app:app . /srv","USER app"] with no accompanying bullets; the concept it illustrates ("UID 1000 inside is UID 1000 outside") is only introduced on page 12.
findings.fix: Move the block to page 12 under "2. Three Ways To Fix It" as the worked example for the `adduser -u 1000 + USER` row.

findings.summary: Page 2's inherited "(cont.)" title misdescribes its content, which is the numeric-UID permission trap rather than namespaces or layers.
findings.evidence: Title: "Namespaces, Layers & The Disposable Container (cont.)"; the page's only block is a bash snippet: "docker exec c ls -lan /data" / "# drwxr-xr-x 2 1000 1000 ...  numeric!" / "# Permission denied = UID mismatch".
findings.fix: Either retitle page 2 to match what it shows (e.g. "Numeric UID On A Mount: The First Symptom") or move that snippet onto page 12 ("Backups & The Numeric UID/GID Traps") where the topic is developed, and let a namespaces/layers block carry the "(cont.)" page.

findings.summary: The symptom table files "different network" under connection refused, but Docker's inter-network isolation rules DROP that traffic, which presents as a timeout.
findings.evidence: Table row: "Refused peer to peer" → "different network, or host port" (repeated on page 5: "Refused between containers: wrong network, or the host-side port"). DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-2 ends in `-j DROP`, so cross-network packets are silently discarded rather than answered with RST; refused means the packet reached a host/container with nothing listening.
findings.fix: Move "different network" to the Timeout row ("firewall, routing, MTU, or cross-network isolation") and leave "Refused peer to peer" as "reached it, nothing listening — wrong port, or a host-bound published port". Apply the same correction to the page-5 bullet.

findings.summary: The `/etc/resolv.conf` / 127.0.0.11 snippet is shown at the end of the drivers page, before the embedded resolver is introduced on the next page.
findings.evidence: Page 8's closing block: "docker exec c cat /etc/resolv.conf" / "# nameserver 127.0.0.11" / "# upstream from --dns or daemon.json", while page 9 states for the first time "Resolver at 127.0.0.11 in every user-defined-network container."
findings.fix: Move that code block to page 9 so it sits immediately after the "6. Embedded DNS Begins" bullets that define 127.0.0.11.

findings.summary: The `--link` callout says the injected entries broke across restarts, but Docker updated linked containers' /etc/hosts on restart — only the environment variables went stale.
findings.evidence: "It injected /etc/hosts entries and env vars, one-directional, and broke across restarts." Docker's legacy-links docs: "If you restart the source container, the /etc/hosts files on the linked containers are automatically updated with the source container's new IP address", while "IP addresses stored in the environment variables are not automatically updated if the source container is restarted."
findings.fix: Change to "...one-directional, and the injected env vars went stale on restart (only /etc/hosts was refreshed)."

findings.summary: The volume-vs-bind decision rule is stated as a takeaway one page before the comparison table that justifies it.
findings.evidence: Page 9 callout "Decision Line": "Bind mount for dev source and host config; named volume for databases and production; tmpfs for secrets and scratch." — the supporting evidence table ["Portability","wins","host-tied"], ["Desktop speed","fast","much slower"] appears on page 10 under "2. Picking Between Them".
findings.fix: Move the "Decision Line" callout to page 10 directly after the Volume-vs-Bind comparison table, or move that table up to page 9 ahead of the callout.

findings.summary: The bullet attributes NFS and CIFS/SMB support to plugins, contradicting the code block directly above it which mounts NFS with the built-in `local` driver.
findings.evidence: Bullet: "`local` is the default; plugins add NFS, CIFS/SMB, cloud disks." Immediately above: "docker volume create --driver local --opt type=nfs --opt device=:/exp/data --opt o=addr=10.0.0.5,rw nfsvol".
findings.fix: Reword to "`local` is the default and already speaks NFS/CIFS via `--opt type=`; plugins add cloud disks and clustered storage."

findings.summary: The yellow sticky-note annotation and its pin overlap the code block it annotates, with the pin sitting on the end of a code line.
findings.evidence: The pin graphic lands directly between "- /app/node_modules" and "# anon", and the note "host dir must not shadow installed modules" is drawn inside the dashed code box boundary.
findings.fix: Offset the sticky note and pin outside the dashed code-block bounds (e.g. to the right margin) so no glyph of "/app/node_modules  # anon" is covered.

findings.summary: The official Postgres image drops privileges with `gosu`, not `su-exec`.
findings.evidence: "Official Postgres starts as root then `su-exec` to postgres." docker-library/postgres `docker-entrypoint.sh` contains `exec gosu postgres "$BASH_SOURCE" "$@"`; the Alpine template installs gosu and only symlinks `su-exec` → `gosu` for backwards compatibility on PG 14–16 (dropped in 17+).
findings.fix: Change to "Official Postgres starts as root then `gosu` to postgres."

findings.summary: Claiming `userns-remap` is the only thing that breaks container-root-equals-host-root omits rootless Docker, which does the same via a user namespace.
findings.evidence: "Only `userns-remap` in daemon.json breaks that equivalence."
findings.fix: Change to "Only `userns-remap` — or running the daemon rootless — breaks that equivalence."

findings.summary: With an unknown UID, `$HOME` is set to `/`, not left unset.
findings.evidence: "`--user` with an unknown UID: `whoami` fails, `$HOME` unset." Docker falls back to the default exec-user home when /etc/passwd has no matching entry, so `docker run -u 4242 alpine env` prints `HOME=/`.
findings.fix: Change to "`whoami` fails and `$HOME` falls back to `/` — an unwritable home, so caches and dotfiles break."
